sentences: I run the lexer over the source file to produce a stream of tokens for the parser.
I check the symbol table to resolve identifiers and ensure each variable is declared before use.
I build an abstract syntax tree from the token sequence and then traverse it for semantic analysis.
I perform type checking on the AST to verify that operands match their operators' expected types.
I generate an intermediate representation in three-address code from the typed abstract syntax tree.
I apply constant folding to the IR to replace expressions with known values at compile time.
I eliminate dead code by removing instructions that have no effect on the program's output.
I inline small functions into their call sites to reduce the overhead of function calls.
I analyze control flow by constructing a directed graph of basic blocks and their edges.
I compute liveness of variables to determine which registers can be reused across instructions.
I allocate registers to variables by building an interference graph and coloring it.
I schedule instructions to minimize pipeline stalls on the target processor architecture.
I emit assembly code for the target machine from the optimized intermediate representation.
I assemble the generated assembly into an object file with relocations and symbol references.
I link the object files with libraries to produce an executable binary for the operating system.
I parse the command-line flags to configure optimization levels and output file paths.
I maintain a hash table for the symbol table to allow fast lookup of variable names.
I handle error recovery in the parser by skipping tokens until a synchronization point.
I generate debug information that maps machine instructions back to source line numbers.
I test the compiler by compiling a suite of programs and comparing the output with a reference.
